summary: Tonga issues a 30-day visitor's visa on arrival to citizens of about 35 countries its Customs and Immigration page lists — among them the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Ireland and many Pacific and Commonwealth states — on the strength of a return ticket and sufficient funds. Citizens of the other 26 EU member states are visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU–Tonga visa waiver agreement. Chinese citizens are visa-free for 30 days under a bilateral agreement. Citizens of every other country need a visa before arrival.

The UK government says the maximum penalty for importing or exporting illegal drugs is 30 years' hard labour and fines of several hundred thousand US dollars.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says most major hotels and some restaurants and stores accept credit cards, that ATMs are available on Tongatapu, especially in Nuku'alofa, and that foreign currency exchange may be limited on the other islands.

safety.text: Tonga is a calm, community-minded country: serious crime is low, but petty theft is fairly common. Natural hazards matter more — cyclones mainly from November to May, and an active volcanic and seismic zone.

tips.text: The UK government says Tongan people strictly observe the Sabbath, and that on Sundays recreational activities may be considered disrespectful, except at island resorts. Plan shopping and activities around it.

The UK government says topless sunbathing and public nudity are illegal, with fines of up to 100 pa'anga, and that swimwear is acceptable on the beach or by streams and waterfalls but likely to attract negative attention elsewhere.

The UK government says it is illegal to swim or kayak with whales unless you are on a licensed boat with a certified guide, with fines of up to 5,000 pa'anga or 18 months in prison. Whales are in Tongan waters between June and November.

The UK government says the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May but cyclones can happen at any time, and that Tonga lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire, where earthquakes and volcanic eruptions can trigger tsunamis. Make sure your insurance covers disruption.

Canada's travel advice says ATMs are available on Tongatapu, especially in Nuku'alofa, and that currency exchange may be limited on other islands. Carry enough pa'anga before you head to the outer islands.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tonga?
faq.answer: Not in advance if your country is on Tonga's list: citizens of the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Singapore, Ireland and many Pacific and Commonwealth countries receive a free 30-day visitor's visa on arrival. Citizens of the other 26 EU member states need no visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU–Tonga visa waiver agreement. Chinese citizens are visa-free for 30 days under a bilateral agreement. Citizens of every other country — including South Korea, Israel, Iceland and Liechtenstein — must obtain a visa before arrival.

faq.question: How long is the visa on arrival valid for?
faq.answer: 30 days. It is issued on arrival on presentation of a passport valid for at least 6 months, a return ticket out of Tonga and evidence of sufficient funds; officers may also ask for confirmed accommodation. To stay longer, apply to the Immigration Department before it expires.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Tonga?
faq.answer: Yes. Apply to the Immigration Department in Nuku'alofa (Salote Road) or Neiafu, Vava'u, before your current visa expires. No official source publishes how long an extension lasts or the maximum total stay.

faq.question: Is everything really closed on Sunday in Tonga?
faq.answer: The UK government says Tongan people strictly observe the Sabbath and that recreational activities on Sundays may be seen as disrespectful, except at island resorts; Canada says such activity outside resorts may be seen as provocative. Plan arrivals, shopping and activities around it.

faq.question: Can I pay by card in Tonga?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says most major hotels and some restaurants and stores accept credit cards, ATMs are available on Tongatapu, especially in Nuku'alofa, and foreign currency exchange may be limited on other islands. Carry pa'anga cash for the outer islands.
